resteasy_liberty_best_practices.overview: Framework-specific best practices for working with RESTeasy, Open Liberty, Jakarta EE, and MicroProfile. These guidelines ensure code quality, maintainability, and proper integration across frameworks.

practice.name: Proper Package Imports and Exports
practice.description: Always declare explicit package imports and exports in bundle manifests. Avoid using wildcards or version ranges that are too broad.
practice.rationale: Explicit declarations prevent classloader issues and make dependencies clear. Proper versioning ensures compatibility across Liberty versions.
practice.good_example:
Import-Package: javax.ws.rs;version="[2.1,3)", javax.ws.rs.core;version="[2.1,3)", org.jboss.resteasy.spi;version="[4.0,5)", javax.enterprise.inject;version="[2.0,3)"
Export-Package: com.ibm.ws.jaxrs.resteasy;version="1.0.0"

practice.name: Bundle Activator Lifecycle Management
practice.description: Implement proper start() and stop() methods in bundle activators. Clean up resources in stop() to prevent memory leaks.

practice.name: OSGi Service Dependencies
practice.description: Use declarative services (DS) annotations for service dependencies. Handle dynamic service availability properly.

practice.name: Proper Bean Scopes
practice.description: Choose appropriate CDI scopes based on bean lifecycle requirements. Avoid using @ApplicationScoped for stateful beans.

scope_guidelines.scope: Use for: Stateless services, configuration holders, caches Thread safety: Must be thread-safe Lifecycle: Lives for entire application
Use for: Request-specific data, JAX-RS resources Thread safety: Not required (single thread per instance) Lifecycle: Created per HTTP request
Use for: User session data Thread safety: Must be thread-safe Lifecycle: Lives for HTTP session duration
Use for: Utility objects, short-lived helpers Thread safety: Depends on usage Lifecycle: Tied to injecting bean

practice.name: CDI Producer Methods
practice.description: Use producer methods for objects that require special initialization or are not CDI beans themselves.

practice.name: Injection Point Validation
practice.description: Validate injection points at deployment time using CDI extensions. Fail fast if required dependencies are missing.

practice.name: Resource Class Design
practice.description: Keep JAX-RS resource classes focused and stateless. Use CDI for dependency injection, not manual instantiation.

practice.name: Exception Mapping
practice.description: Implement ExceptionMapper for consistent error handling. Map framework exceptions to appropriate HTTP responses.

practice.name: Provider Ordering
practice.description: Use @Priority to control provider execution order. Lower numbers execute first for filters, last for interceptors.

practice.name: Async Resource Methods
practice.description: Use async processing for long-running operations. Properly manage thread pools and timeouts.

practice.name: Config Property Injection
practice.description: Use MicroProfile Config for externalized configuration. Provide sensible defaults and document required properties.

practice.name: Health Check Implementation
practice.description: Implement health checks for critical dependencies. Distinguish between liveness and readiness probes.

practice.name: Metrics Annotations
practice.description: Use MicroProfile Metrics to expose application metrics. Choose appropriate metric types for different measurements.

practice.name: Feature Manifest Structure
practice.description: Create well-structured feature manifests with clear dependencies. Use subsystem content for proper feature composition.
practice.good_example:
Subsystem-SymbolicName: com.example.myfeature-1.0 Subsystem-Version: 1.0.0 Subsystem-Type: osgi.subsystem.feature IBM-ShortName: myFeature-1.0 IBM-API-Package: com.example.api; type="api"
IBM-Feature-Version: 2
-features=\ com.ibm.websphere.appserver.servlet-4.0,\ com.ibm.websphere.appserver.cdi-2.0,\ com.ibm.websphere.appserver.jaxrs-2.1
-bundles=\ com.example.myfeature.bundle

practice.name: API Package Visibility
practice.description: Clearly define which packages are API vs. internal. Use IBM-API-Package to expose public APIs.
practice.guideline: API packages: Stable, versioned, documented SPI packages: For extension points Internal packages: Implementation details, may change

practice.name: Framework Exception Handling
practice.description: Handle framework-specific exceptions appropriately. Don't swallow exceptions that indicate serious problems.

practice.name: Resource Cleanup
practice.description: Always clean up resources in finally blocks or try-with-resources. Unregister services and close connections properly.

practice.name: Thread Safety in Shared Beans
practice.description: Ensure thread safety for @ApplicationScoped and @SessionScoped beans. Use proper synchronization or concurrent collections.

practice.name: Managed Executor Usage
practice.description: Use Liberty's ManagedExecutorService for async operations. Don't create your own thread pools.

pitfall.name: Classloader Issues
pitfall.description: Classes not visible across bundle boundaries
pitfall.solution: Check Import-Package declarations and ensure proper package exports. Verify bundle wiring with OSGi console commands.

pitfall.name: CDI Scope Mismatches
pitfall.description: Injecting shorter-scoped bean into longer-scoped bean
pitfall.solution: Use CDI proxies or Instance<T> for dynamic lookup. Match bean scopes appropriately.

pitfall.name: Service Circular Dependencies
pitfall.description: OSGi services with circular dependencies fail to start
pitfall.solution: Break circular dependencies by using optional references or events. Redesign service boundaries if necessary.

pitfall.name: Configuration Property Not Found
pitfall.solution: Provide default values or make properties optional. Check property sources and precedence.

category.name: OSGi
category.item: Bundle manifest has explicit imports and exports

category.name: JAX-RS
category.item: Exception mappers handle all error cases

category.name: MicroProfile
category.item: Config properties have defaults or are documented
Health checks distinguish liveness vs readiness

practice.name: Source Attribution
practice.description: Always include a source attribution comment linking to the specific commit in the RESTEasy repository. This enables tracking of upstream changes and understanding the provenance of overlay files.
practice.rationale: Commit-based links are immutable and provide exact version tracking, unlike tag-based links which can change if tags are moved.

practice.name: Copyright Headers
practice.description: All overlay files must include the standard IBM EPL-2.0 copyright header before the source attribution comment.
practice.good_example: /******************************************************************************* * Copyright (c) 2026 IBM Corporation and others. * All rights reserved. This program and the accompanying materials * are made available under the terms of the Eclipse Public License 2.0 * which accompanies this distribution, and is available at * http://www.eclipse.org/legal/epl-2.0/ * * SPDX-License-Identifier: EPL-2.0 *******************************************************************************/ // Source: https://github.com/resteasy/resteasy/blob/abc123.../resteasy-core-spi/src/main/java/org/jboss/resteasy/spi/util/Utils.java package org.jboss.resteasy.spi.util;

practice.name: Version Consistency
practice.description: Ensure overlay files match the RESTEasy version specified in the bundle's bnd.bnd file. Mixing versions can lead to compatibility issues.
practice.verification: Always check the resteasy-version property in bnd.bnd before pulling overlay files to ensure you're using the correct version tag.

practice.name: Module Identification
practice.description: Correctly identify which RESTEasy module contains the file you need. RESTEasy is split into multiple Maven modules (resteasy-core, resteasy-core-spi, resteasy-client, resteasy-cdi, etc.).
practice.tip: Use package prefixes as a guide: - org.jboss.resteasy.spi.* → resteasy-core-spi - org.jboss.resteasy.core.* → resteasy-core - org.jboss.resteasy.client.* → resteasy-client - org.jboss.resteasy.cdi.* → resteasy-cdi

practice.name: Mark Liberty Changes with Standard Comments
practice.description: All Liberty-specific modifications to overlay files MUST be marked with standard Liberty Change comments. This is required for tracking differences from upstream RESTEasy code.

comment_format.single_line: Use for single-line changes: // Liberty Change

practice.rationale: These markers make it easy to: - Identify all Liberty-specific changes when updating to newer RESTEasy versions - Understand what needs to be preserved during updates - Generate diffs showing only Liberty modifications - Review changes for correctness and necessity

practice.name: Document Why Changes Were Made
practice.description: In addition to marking changes, add explanatory comments describing why the Liberty-specific change was necessary.
practice.suggestion: Combine Liberty Change markers with explanatory comments: // Liberty Change: Use Liberty's class loading to support OSGi bundles

practice.name: Update Tracking
practice.description: When updating an existing overlay file to a newer RESTEasy version, review the changes between versions to ensure Liberty modifications are preserved or adapted as needed.
practice.workflow: 1. Note the old commit hash from the source attribution 2. Get the new commit hash for the updated version 3. Compare the two versions on GitHub 4. Reapply any Liberty-specific modifications 5. Update the source attribution comment
